newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Conference organiser arrested by Mauritius police.
newsitem.headline: Conference organiser arrested by Mauritius police.

text.p: The organiser of a major Oil and Minerals conference in Mauritius last week was arrested by Mauritian police at the weekend and was being held on criminal charges, his wife said.
Humphrey Harrison, managing director of Europe Energy Environment which organised the three-day conference at Grand Baie, was arrested with his wife Karin on Saturday.
She told Reuters Mauritius government officials and hotel staff refused to accept payment for outstanding conference bills through bank transfer and insisted on cash.
"On Saturday afternoon my husband and myself were arrested," she said.

She was released later in the day after pleading with police to let her return to her Johannesburg home to attend to her three young children. She paid a portion of the bill on her personal credit card.
Her husband appeared in court on Monday on charges of conspiring to fraudently obtain credit, and the case was postponed to June 30.
She said payment of around 30,000 pounds -- mainly for catering costs -- was made by bank transfer to the hotel on Monday morning.
"There was no problem in transferring the money, the money has been paid," Harrison said.

She said a top Mauritius lawyer had been hired to secure the release of her husband, who was still being held on Tuesday morning, and the South African High Commission on the island had been notified.
The conference is a showcase for sub-Saharan oil and mining with several African ministers attending. It was held for the fourth time this year.
